properties.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #1: caves carved into Navajo sandstone in the 1970s to harvest sand for glassmaking — now a free, photogenic scramble right off Highway 89, about 1.2 miles round trip with parking by the highway. Her caution: the scramble up can get a little scary; don't be afraid to turn back.
properties.creator: @giselle.on.trails
properties.reel_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

properties.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #3: no hiking required if you have a 4x4 (don't attempt it in a normal car) — a 5.3-mile dirt road, about 45 minutes, to falls that pour over two pour-offs on La Verkin Creek: a cascade section and a clean 20-foot drop into a pool. Free BLM land, and the swimming is incredible in summer.
properties.creator: @giselle.on.trails
properties.reel_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

properties.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #4 — her favorite of the five: a permitted slot-canyon waterfall hike, about 3.8 miles out and back with creek crossings the whole way and a ladder climb in the canyon. Permits sell out 1–2 weeks ahead in summer, so book early — and rent the waders unless you want numb feet for an hour afterwards.
properties.creator: @giselle.on.trails
properties.reel_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

properties.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #5: a 4.25-mile out-and-back hike (about 500 ft of gain) that ends up looking like a mini version of Zion's Subway — and a pretty easy one. This is the one she says legit looks like the Subway.
properties.creator: @giselle.on.trails
properties.reel_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

properties.recommendation: Giselle's Zion alternative #2: a 1.2-mile round-trip slot canyon with glowing orange and pink walls. Park at the water facility at the end of Red Hollow Drive — and note the sandy road is popular with off-roaders, so it can be soft going.
properties.creator: @giselle.on.trails
properties.reel_title: When Zion is too packed — 5 spots about an hour away (Kanab area)

Their practical notes: on the road toward the Mars Desert Research Station; unpaved access, high-clearance 4WD recommended; best at sunrise or sunset when low light brings out the colours; and never after rain — wet bentonite turns extremely slippery and sticky and vehicles get stuck.
properties.creator: @megsandpat
properties.reel_title: Bentonite Hills — a landscape from another planet

Its tip: the road is paved for the first stretch, then turns to dirt; past that point you want high clearance or 4WD toward Thelma & Louise Point and the Shafer Trail.

properties.reel_title: Everyone heads to Arches — this scenic byway (Highway 279) packs in so much more

properties.recommendation: Gwyn and Ami's pick for some of the best panoramic mountain views in the North Cascades: Trappers Peak via Thornton Lakes — 9.7 miles with 3,438 ft of gain to stunning 360° summit views. Non-technical (no special gear or skills), with a few steep rock-scramble sections. Their tips: pack plenty of water (few places to filter), no backpacking on the peak itself, and Thornton Lakes backpacking is by competitive NPS permit.
properties.creator: @gwynandami
properties.reel_title: Trappers Peak — 360° views of the North Cascades

properties.recommendation: American Travel Archives' 'you will NOT believe this road' drive: the Million Dollar Highway (US-550) from Ouray to Silverton — 25 miles through the San Juan Mountains famous for steep cliffs, tight switchbacks and few guardrails. Stop at Red Mountain Pass for the classic overlook; autumn is the best time, when golden aspens contrast with the red and gray rock. Their tips: drive it in good morning light, take your time at the pull-offs, and think twice in an RV. Ouray and Silverton bookend it with hot springs and silver-mining history.
properties.creator: @americantravelarchives
properties.reel_title: Million Dollar Highway (US-550) — Ouray to Silverton, CO

properties.recommendation: Jackie's verdict: 'TOTALLY worth it.' Spooky Gulch is the ultra-narrow Dry Fork slot canyon — the trailhead even has a metal frame you must fit through to enter. Inside: twisty sandstone walls, fun downclimbs, a sketchy up-climb to a section she calls 'INTO THE ARCHES', and squeezes so tight she had to take her backpack off and turn sideways.
properties.creator: @jackie.travel.photos
properties.reel_title: Spooky Canyon in Utah!

properties.recommendation: Calvin hiked the Franconia Ridge Trail in July — the classic above-treeline ridge walk across Little Haystack, Mount Lincoln and Mount Lafayette in Franconia Notch. His caution: check the weather and conditions before hiking it in fall or winter, and be prepared — the ridge is fully exposed.
properties.creator: @calvin_on_the_internet
properties.reel_title: Franconia Ridge Trail in New Hampshire

properties.recommendation: Dave & Joce's pick for one of the most iconic sunrises in the U.S.: Cadillac Mountain, famous for being one of the first places in the country to see the sunrise during parts of the year. If you're driving up, vehicle reservations are required during the reservation season — or you can hike to the top.
properties.creator: @daveandjoce
properties.reel_title: Acadia's iconic sunrises — Cadillac Mountain & the Beehive

properties.recommendation: The Trekking Mama's 'how is this real?' lake: Snow Lake looks like it should require a plane ticket or a major expedition, but the trailhead is only about 60 minutes from Seattle. The water is an unbelievable bright alpine blue that looks photoshopped but isn't. It's popular and you'll share the trail — her tip is to keep going past the first viewpoints down toward the end of the lake, where the crowds thin out. Her go-to when someone visits Washington and needs a massive dose of alpine gorgeousness without planning a whole trip.
properties.creator: @the.trekking.mama
properties.reel_title: Snow Lake — the 'how is this real?' lake an hour from Seattle

properties.recommendation: The Griffins' verdict: even on a foggy day, Cape Flattery was unforgettable — the farthest northwest point of the Olympic Peninsula (and the contiguous U.S.), and one of those places that's worth going out of your way for.
properties.creator: @griffins.onthego
properties.reel_title: Cape Flattery, Washington State

properties.recommendation: Giselle calls it 'the final boss of PNW-maxxing' — the most northwestern place in the lower 48. The hike is 1.5 miles round trip with about 200 ft of gain: forest trails, boardwalks, stairs and multiple ocean viewpoints. A Makah Recreation Permit is required (online or in Neah Bay before the trailhead); open daily from dawn until 30 minutes after sunset, year-round. Her tips: it's a remote drive with spotty cell service, so download directions ahead, bring a rain jacket, and stay on the designated trails and viewing platforms.
properties.creator: @giselle.on.trails
properties.reel_title: Cape Flattery — the final boss of PNW-maxxing

properties.recommendation: Calvin's pick: the Ice Lake Basin Trail outside Silverton, Colorado — the San Juan Mountains' famous alpine basin of electric-blue lakes (Ice Lake and Island Lake) ringed by 13,000-foot peaks.
properties.creator: @calvin_on_the_internet
properties.reel_title: Ice Lake Basin Trail — Silverton, Colorado

properties.recommendation: Lindsay & Ryan: 'There's nowhere else on earth quite like this national park' — step back in time and explore the incredible cliff dwellings built by the Ancestral Pueblo people. Their plan: stay at Morefield Campground as the home base inside the park, start at the Visitor & Research Center to learn the history and plan the visit, book ranger-guided tours through Recreation.gov to get up close to the dwellings (they loved Cliff Palace and Balcony House), and grab fry bread at Soda Point after a day of exploring.
properties.creator: @throughourlinds
properties.reel_title: Mesa Verde — cliff dwellings, Cliff Palace & Balcony House

properties.recommendation: The largest cliff dwelling in North America — and one of the two Mesa Verde dwellings Lindsay & Ryan loved exploring on a ranger-guided tour (booked through Recreation.gov to get up close).
properties.creator: @throughourlinds
properties.reel_title: Mesa Verde — cliff dwellings, Cliff Palace & Balcony House

properties.recommendation: Lindsay & Ryan's other favorite Mesa Verde dwelling tour (ranger-guided, booked through Recreation.gov) — Balcony House, the park's most adventurous dwelling visit, reached by ladders and a tunnel crawl.
properties.creator: @throughourlinds
properties.reel_title: Mesa Verde — cliff dwellings, Cliff Palace & Balcony House

properties.recommendation: Big Bat Billy's stop: the Tree of Life at Kalaloch Beach in Olympic National Park — the famous Sitka spruce that keeps growing over an eroded gully, its roots exposed in a root cave beneath it, right on the beach.
properties.creator: @bigbatbilly
properties.reel_title: Tree of Life — Kalaloch Beach, Olympic National Park

properties.recommendation: Jess drove 9 hours to camp on the Alvord Desert playa — under some of the darkest skies in Oregon — to teach herself astrophotography. She timed the trip under an almost-full moon by accident, so she waited for moonset, set a 3:24 AM alarm, and manually shot 105 long exposures (her old Sony has no intervalometer) to stitch a four-second starlapse. Her verdict: the Alvord had been on her list a long time and was worth every bit of the drive.
properties.creator: @jessonthewildway
properties.reel_title: Alvord Desert — a 3:24 AM starlapse on the playa

properties.recommendation: A cave hiding in the Illinois woods: Whipple's Cave in Franklin Creek State Natural Area, reached via the Pioneer Pass Trail from the Mill Springs Day Use Area — 2.9 miles out and back with 226 ft of gain through wooded scenery, rocky terrain and creek crossings. Know before you go: be prepared for deep creek crossings, and other trails in the area also lead to the cave.
properties.creator: @our.adventure.tails
properties.reel_title: Whipple's Cave — a cave hiding in the Illinois woods

properties.recommendation: Andrew's take: 'Some places make you stop and appreciate just how beautiful the world really is.' Lake of the Clouds, tucked in the heart of Michigan's Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park, is one of those places that never fails to impress — his photos catch it in full fall color.
properties.creator: @andrew_krzesinski
properties.reel_title: Lake of the Clouds — Porcupine Mountains, Michigan

properties.recommendation: Amory's #4 unique national park waterfall: Hidden Falls in Glacier — a powerful waterfall plunging through a narrow, mossy rock gorge, with snow-capped peaks and evergreens behind it.
properties.creator: @amorywild
properties.reel_title: Top 5 Unique National Park Waterfalls

properties.recommendation: Amory's #3 unique national park waterfall: Zapata Falls near Great Sand Dunes — a dramatic falls hidden inside a dark rock cavern at the foot of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, shown as a frozen icefall in winter.
properties.creator: @amorywild
properties.reel_title: Top 5 Unique National Park Waterfalls

properties.recommendation: Amory's #1 unique national park waterfall: Brooks Falls in Katmai — the famous falls where brown bears stand in the river catching leaping salmon.
properties.creator: @amorywild
properties.reel_title: Top 5 Unique National Park Waterfalls

properties.recommendation: WTA calls Mount Si the most popular hike in Washington — upwards of 100,000 hikers a year. The switchbacks start right at the trailhead; a mile and a half up you pass through Snag Flat, old-growth trees that survived fire and logging, then past a talus slope to the base of the Haystack, the true summit. 8.0 miles round trip with 3,150 ft of gain. Climbers training for Rainier haul heavy packs up here — the rule of thumb is that if you can make the top in under two hours, you're ready. A Discover Pass is required to park, and the lot fills early.
properties.creator: @outdoorsapp
properties.reel_title: Mount Si — Washington's most popular hike

properties.recommendation: Amory's #5 unique national park waterfall: Wolf Creek Falls in New River Gorge — a wide, moss-covered cascade where water seeps and sheets over rocks beside the hiking trail.
properties.creator: @amorywild
properties.reel_title: Top 5 Unique National Park Waterfalls

properties.recommendation: Amory's #2 unique national park waterfall: Cataract Falls in Kenai Fjords — massive waterfalls pouring down sheer coastal cliffs directly into the ocean, seen from a boat.
properties.creator: @amorywild
properties.reel_title: Top 5 Unique National Park Waterfalls

properties.recommendation: A 1/4-mile walk on Princess Arch Trail (#233) to Princess Arch, a natural sandstone arch in Red River Gorge — the reel hikes it at peak fall color, with a sandstone ledge overlook above a valley of red and gold trees on the way.
properties.creator: @jhunjhun_jn8888
properties.reel_title: Princess Arch Trail in fall — Red River Gorge

properties.recommendation: One of the most unique swims in the Midwest: hundreds of natural pools and chutes the Black River carved into billion-year-old volcanic rock — 'nature's own waterpark,' about 2 hours south of St. Louis. The reel's tips: go early in summer (it gets busy), wear water shoes for the slippery rock, and mind the stronger currents with kids.
properties.creator: @coupleofpatels
properties.reel_title: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park — nature's waterpark in Missouri

properties.recommendation: 'This state park surprised us': 14+ miles of trails with caves to explore, an astronomy center that's perfect for stargazing, and four campgrounds on the bluffs near Bagley. Day pass $13 in-state / $16 out-of-state, per the reel.
properties.creator: @thekateandcody
properties.reel_title: This state park surprised us — Wyalusing State Park, Wisconsin

properties.recommendation: The creators' favorite trail in the park: the Old Immigrant & Bluff Loop — the hike the reel films, past a natural-arch rock formation and up wooden stairs built against the cliff to a cave with sandy floors, crawl spaces, and openings that look out over the forest.
properties.creator: @thekateandcody
properties.reel_title: This state park surprised us — Wyalusing State Park, Wisconsin

properties.recommendation: It looks like Hawaii's Stairway to Heaven, but it's just north of San Francisco: an easy climb of about 650 steps from the parking area to panoramic views — the Pacific on one side, the Golden Gate Bridge on the other. No long hike, free parking off Conzelman Road.
properties.creator: @anjali_wandersoul
properties.reel_title: Hawk Hill — a 'Stairway to Heaven' viewpoint over the Golden Gate

properties.recommendation: One of Asya's five favorite California drives: Highway 395 along the Eastern Sierra — a winding road under snow-capped peaks and pine forests, with the Sierra escarpment on one side and the high desert on the other.
properties.creator: @asyatravels
properties.reel_title: 5 Most Scenic Drives in California

properties.recommendation: One of the five: the 17-Mile Drive through Pebble Beach — a tree-lined coastal road the reel shows bathed in golden sunset light, past cypress trees and ocean viewpoints.
properties.creator: @asyatravels
properties.reel_title: 5 Most Scenic Drives in California

properties.recommendation: One of the five: the Kings Canyon Scenic Byway — a narrow road carved between steep rocky canyon walls as it descends into Kings Canyon, following the Kings River toward Roads End.
properties.creator: @asyatravels
properties.reel_title: 5 Most Scenic Drives in California

properties.recommendation: One of the five: driving through Jedediah Smith Redwoods — a dense forest of towering old-growth redwoods, the reel's lush green counterpoint to the desert and coast drives.
properties.creator: @asyatravels
properties.reel_title: 5 Most Scenic Drives in California

properties.recommendation: One of the five, and the caption's headliner: Big Sur — Highway 1 along green grassy cliffs above the Pacific and its rocky shoreline, the most famous coastal drive in California.
properties.creator: @asyatravels
properties.reel_title: 5 Most Scenic Drives in California

properties.creator: @discover_california_
properties.reel_title: 7 hikes that will ruin every other hike for you

properties.recommendation: A surreal chain of smooth white-granite pools on Dry Meadow Creek, each cup dropping 6 to 20 feet into the next before the water slides into the Kern River. Reached by a roughly 4-mile round-trip hike with about 850 feet of gain, rock scrambling and a creek crossing. The creator's warning, kept verbatim in spirit: please don't swim — the current can pull swimmers under even when the water looks calm.
properties.creator: @asyatravels
properties.reel_title: Seven Teacups — granite pools above the Kern River

properties.recommendation: The 'Caribbean of the Midwest' in autumn: Torch Lake's turquoise, crystal-clear water and shallow sandbars ringed by peak fall color — the reel's drone shots show deep blue open water against shores of red and gold. The caption pitches the area's wineries and orchards as a perfect Michigan fall road trip.
properties.creator: @marco.horizons
properties.reel_title: Torch Lake in Fall feels like the movies

properties.best_for: Hike · Sand dune climb, tide pools and coastal views
properties.recommendation: Climb the 240-foot sand dune for the payoff view over sandstone cliffs, tide pools and sandy beaches, with Pacific City's own Haystack Rock offshore. There's also an easier 1-mile walk along the beach to the rocks of the cape.
properties.creator: @lauren_see
properties.reel_title: Cape Kiwanda — 12/10 view on the Oregon Coast

properties.best_for: Cave tour · America's only all-water cavern, toured by boat
properties.recommendation: The reel's first stop: a boat ride through America's only all-water cavern — you float the underground river past illuminated stalactites instead of walking. It's also the only Pennsylvania cave on the National Register of Historic Places, with a wildlife park above ground.
properties.creator: @hunterhulbert
properties.reel_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2

properties.recommendation: A 300-million-year-old sandstone 'rock city' in Clearfield County — moss-covered boulders split into narrow passageways and small caves; the reel's presenter squeezes through the crevices and wanders the forest among the rocks.
properties.creator: @hunterhulbert
properties.reel_title: Pennsylvania Road Trip Ideas Part 2

properties.recommendation: The reel stops in Elk County near Benezette for Pennsylvania's wild elk herd — wide fields at sunrise and sunset and a big bull elk filmed from the roadside. The Elk Country Visitor Center on Winslow Hill is the hub of the viewing area.
properties.creator: @hunterhulbert

properties.best_for: Hike · Short historic stone-step path to Dorr Mountain
properties.recommendation: One of the shortest hikes in Acadia National Park might also be one of the most unique: tucked into the Sieur de Monts area near Bar Harbor, Homans Path is just 0.3 miles one way (0.8 mi out-and-back with ~334 ft of climb) but packs in intricate granite staircases, narrow forest passages, historic stonework, a stone 'hallway' and beautiful views on a short but steep climb. The reel pairs it into a half-day Sieur de Monts itinerary: Wild Gardens of Acadia, the Nature Center, the Jesup Path boardwalk, then Homans Path, with the Island Explorer shuttle as an option. The path is a memorial trail honoring Eliza Lothrop Homans' land donations; it joins the Schiff Path toward the summit of Dorr Mountain.

properties.best_for: Slot canyon / Guided tour · Antelope-style canyon without the crowds
properties.recommendation: The reel's pitch: people pay hundreds to visit Antelope Canyon, but almost no one knows about this slot canyon near Zion — towering red sandstone walls (100+ ft high, 6–10 ft wide), winding passageways and incredible photo opportunities WITHOUT the crowds. The catch, stated honestly in the reel: Crimson Canyon itself has no entrance fee, but you can't access it independently because the route crosses private property — you book a guided tour with a company that has permission. They booked East Zion Adventures and loved it: a ~2-hour trip, UTV ride into the backcountry from Orderville, then a guided hike with short climbs (obstacles up to ~10 ft).

properties.best_for: Hike / Summit · Bare rocky summit with 360° views
properties.recommendation: Calvin's reel takes on Mt. Monadnock in southern New Hampshire — the 3,165-ft peak that gave 'monadnock' its name (an isolated mountain rising from the plain), reputed to be one of the most-climbed mountains in the world. The classic route is the White Dot Trail up from the state park headquarters (3.4–3.6 mi round trip, ~1,750 ft gain, with rock scrambles and stone steps) and down the White Cross — the bare, rocky summit opens to sweeping views across southern New Hampshire and, on clear days, all six New England states. A National Natural Landmark with a literary streak: Emerson and Thoreau both climbed and wrote about it. No dogs allowed on the mountain.

properties.recommendation: Known as the '8th Wonder of the World' (Theodore Roosevelt's phrase): Burney Falls, just outside the tiny town of Burney, California — and it's only a short walk from the parking lot. The 129-foot falls push through about 100 million gallons of water a day, and because they're mainly fed by underground springs they flow all year round. A little over an hour from Redding, which the reel suggests as home base. Note from the reel: during peak summer season, weekend visits need a reservation booked in advance (none needed after late September).
